explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 41 named tracks and releases across current 2026 review windows, adjacent bass/house/electro material and overlooked 2009–2016 catalogue sources; metadata and attributed descriptions only; no audio audition.
exclusions: All canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects, untriggered PARKED revisits, previously retained exact identities and previously unresolved leads lacking materially new identity evidence were excluded.
The two listener-protected internal trio handoffs remain unavailable; Truth in Noise → Transparency and all other boundaries are not protected by implication.
The current 17-track length and three consecutive internal ADDs were treated as cumulative-journey scrutiny, not as an automatic moratorium or quota.
No track was promoted from BPM, prestige, genre label or novelty alone; no exact energy, density, perceived pulse, phrase structure or mixability was inferred.
Nine honest contenders survived the scan; the count was not padded.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. Picture — Wooooooo: current boundary-scale contender whose exact wind-to-hardgroove-bassline development could form a deliberate afterword or overture.
2. Decoder — Abundance: current controlled-continuation contender whose exact swung, funked-up beat evidence may deepen an early run without requiring another conspicuous mechanism.
3. Batu & Donato Dozzy — Flickers: current structural contender whose bouncy kick cedes to a rubbery gong, offering an early widening or unprotected threshold.
4. Stephen Brown — Mini Mood: overlooked techno construction where a second kick explicitly turns circular motion into a swung surge.
5. Ploy — Admirer: adjacent hardgroove/house contender with exact swung chromatic drums and bodily funk.
6. DJ Sotofett Meets Abu Sayah — Houran (Percussion Mix): adjacent polyrhythmic broken-house construction and possible different-world boundary move.
7. Mor Elian — Basma: lean exact drum/bass construction with a possible early or tail function.
8. Acre — Jouska: heavily swung adjacent-world contender ranked lower because techno belonging is less direct.
9. 2562 — Like A Dream: overlooked bass-techno hybrid ranked lower because its distinct gain for the current journey is less clear.
